h: A Whole Day at the Trafford Centre and Trafford Quays
p: The Trafford Centre is so much more than a shopping trip, and Thrill Coaster slots neatly into a full family day. The Orient food court, designed to look like the deck of an ocean liner with a mix of styles from around the world, is a sight in itself and has plenty of choice for fussy eaters. It's a good place to sit down and refuel between activities.

Families with younger kids have other options right on site. LEGOLAND Discovery Centre Manchester is packed with LEGO builds, a 4D cinema and play areas, and SEA LIFE Manchester has tanks full of sharks, rays and other marine creatures. Combining a couple of these with a quick go on Thrill Coaster can make for a cracking rainy-day itinerary, all under one roof.

Just across the road at Trafford Quays, Chill Factore has an indoor real-snow slope, where you can have a ski or snowboarding lesson, or go sledging and tubing in the snow park. It's an unusual way to round off a day, especially in the middle of summer.

A few practical bits for Thrill Coaster itself. Height and age limits may apply, so check before you queue, especially with younger children. If you get motion sick easily, avoid going straight after a big meal, and remember you can always stop if it gets too much. Glasses usually fit under the headset, but ask the staff if you're unsure.

Getting to the Trafford Centre is easy. The Metrolink tram line from Manchester city centre runs right to the Trafford Centre, and there's plenty of free parking for drivers. If you want to make a weekend of it, Salford Quays isn't far away, home to IWM North, the striking war museum designed by Daniel Libeskind, and The Lowry arts centre, named after the famous painter of matchstick figures.
